---
title: Formatting
---

`biblint format` writes a canonical representation of the BibTeX it understands.
It is deliberately conservative: the default profile changes presentation, not the spelling of bibliographic values or the identity of entries.

Use `--diff` to preview a change, `--check` to make formatting a CI gate, and no flag to write the configured profile:

```console
biblint format references.bib --diff
```

The command above prints a unified diff and leaves `references.bib` untouched.
Once the diff is acceptable, run `biblint format references.bib` to write it.

## Default shape

Input:

```bibtex
@ARTICLE{Smith2024,
author={Smith, John},
title={A Study},
year=2024
}
```

Default output:

```bibtex
@article{Smith2024,
  author = {Smith, John},
  title = {A Study},
  year = 2024
}
```

The default profile lowercases entry types and field names, uses two-space indentation, and separates entries with a blank line.
It does not align equals signs, sort entries or fields, add braces, change values, or remove duplicate and empty fields.

## Layout and ordering

Set layout preferences under `[format]`:

```toml
[format]
indent = 2                 # a space count, or "tab"
align = false              # or a field-name column number
blank-lines = true
lowercase = true
trailing-commas = true
wrap = 80                  # false disables wrapping
sort = ["key"]             # true uses key order
sort-fields = ["title", "author", "year"]
```

`sort` controls entry order.
`sort-fields` controls field order within each entry; `true` uses biblint's built-in field order.
Lists provide an explicit order, and fields not named in a list remain after the named fields.

## Value transforms

These options change value spelling or representation, so enable them only when that is part of the repository's policy:

| Setting     | Effect                                                     |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `curly`        | Enclose values in braces.                                  |
| `numeric`        | Render numeric values as bare literals.                    |
| `months`        | Normalize recognized month names.                          |
| `format-page-ranges`        | Normalize page ranges.                                     |
| `escape` / `unescape` | Convert supported text between Unicode and LaTeX.          |
| `encode-urls`        | Encode URL underscores.                                    |
| `strip-enclosing-braces`        | Remove one outer brace group.                              |
| `enclosing-braces` / `remove-braces` | Select fields whose brace depth changes.                   |
| `drop-all-caps`        | Convert all-caps values to title case.                     |
| `wrap`        | Wrap long values at a configured width.                    |
| `lowercase`        | Lowercase entry types and field names; enabled by default. |

The escape table is package-independent.
Characters that have no built-in LaTeX escape are preserved and reported by `unsupported_escape` when the relevant check is enabled.

## Cleanup and semantic transforms

Use these settings when you intentionally want to remove, merge, or otherwise change data:

```toml
[format]
remove-empty-fields = true
remove-duplicate-fields = true
omit = ["abstract"]
strip-comments = true
tidy-comments = true
max-authors = 3
generate-keys = true
duplicate-kinds = ["doi", "citation"]
merge = "combine"
```

`merge` accepts `first`, `last`, `combine`, and `overwrite`.
When `duplicate-kinds` is empty, merging considers DOI, citation, and abstract duplicates.
Add `key` if key duplicates should also be merged.
Without a `merge` strategy, duplicate entries are preserved.

`generate-keys` uses the same formula evaluator as the `key_format` rule.
See [Citekey generation](key-generation.md) for the supported Better BibTeX syntax.

## Fix safety

`check --format --fix` applies the formatting diagnostic only when formatting is enabled, and it applies safe fixes by default.
Add `--unsafe-fixes` when the configured profile includes a transform that can remove information or change entry identity:

```console
biblint check references.bib --format --fix --unsafe-fixes
```

This safety gate covers citekey generation, merging, omission or removal of fields/braces/comments, all-caps conversion, unescaping, duplicate/empty-field cleanup, and author truncation.
The standalone `format` command applies the configured profile directly, so preview it with `--diff` first.

## Preserved source

Comments, special entries, and unstructured source are retained unless a configured transform targets them.
Unstructured source is reported as `unsupported_construct` rather than discarded.
